title: Thermal phase transitions in a mixed-spin Ising model on the Lieb lattice: Exact results beyond zero magnetic field
abstract: We investigate the ground-state and finite-temperature properties of a mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1 Ising model on a decorated square (Lieb) lattice incorporating a uniaxial single-ion anisotropy and magnetic field. By employing the generalized decoration-iteration transformation, the model is mapped exactly onto an effective spin-1/2 Ising model on the square lattice characterized by an effective nearest-neighbor interaction and an effective field. The studied model consequently becomes exactly solvable even for finite values of the applied magnetic field whenever the effective field vanishes. The ground-state analysis reveals three distinct phases: ferrimagnetic phase (FRI), disordered phase (DP), and ferromagnetic (FM) phase. The ground-state boundary between FRI and DP phases gives rise to a dome-shaped surface of discontinuous thermal phase transitions, which is terminated by a line of Ising-type critical points associated with continuous thermal phase transitions. Both continuous and discontinuous thermal phase transitions belong to the exactly solvable parameter regime defined by a vanishing effective field in spite of the fact that the applied magnetic field is finite. Two consecutive discontinuous thermally-induced reentrant phase transitions DP-FRI-DP are identified in a narrow parameter region. The exact analytical predictions including reentrance, field- and thermally-driven phase transitions are independently verified by classical Monte Carlo simulations.
summary: This work analyzes the phase transitions of a mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1 Ising model on a Lieb lattice using an exact mapping technique. The methodology reduces the complex system to an effective 2D Ising model, enabling analytical predictions for ground states and thermal behavior. Key findings include identifying multiple distinct phases and observing reentrant thermal transitions under specific field conditions.
main_problem: The study investigates the ground-state and finite-temperature phase transitions of a mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1 Ising model on a Lieb lattice.
main_result: The system exhibits three distinct ground-state phases (FRI, DP, FM) and displays complex thermal behavior, including dome-shaped surfaces of discontinuous transitions and reentrant $	ext{DP} 	o 	ext{FRI} 	o 	ext{DP}$ sequences.
method: The authors employ the generalized decoration-iteration transformation to map the mixed-spin model exactly onto an effective spin-1/2 Ising model on a square lattice, allowing for exact analytical solutions.
model_or_system: The system is a mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1 Ising model defined on a decorated square (Lieb) lattice. The Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor interactions, uniaxial single-ion anisotropy ($D$), and an external magnetic field ($h$).
key_observables: Ground state phase boundaries (FRI, DP, FM), critical temperatures, magnetization ($m_\sigma, m_S, m_T$), and susceptibility ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Anisotropy ratio ($D/J$) and magnetic field ratio ($h/J$); the analysis focuses on regimes where the effective field $h_{	ext{eff}}$ vanishes.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the generalized decoration-iteration transformation provides an exact mapping, allowing all thermodynamic properties to be derived from the solvable effective model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ground-state phase diagram in the $D/J$-$h/J$ plane showing three phases; thermal diagrams show a dome of discontinuous transitions bounded by continuous critical lines; and magnetization plots confirm reentrant behavior across varying magnetic fields.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the mixed-spin Hamiltonian on the Lieb lattice. It then details the exact mapping via decoration-iteration to an effective square lattice model. Subsequently, it analyzes ground-state phase boundaries and finally explores finite-temperature transitions, identifying continuous critical lines and reentrant discontinuous regimes.
why_interesting: The ability to map a complex mixed-spin system onto a solvable 2D Ising model provides powerful analytical tools for understanding frustrated or multi-component magnetic systems relevant in condensed matter physics.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Zero-temperature density plots of the effective magnetic field heff/J (a) and the effective interaction Jeff/J (b) in the D/J −h/J plane. The solid black lines represent ground-state phase boundaries separating the ferrimagnetic (FRI), disordered (DP), and ferromagnetic (FM) phases.

Figure 4: Global phase diagram of the mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1 Ising model on the Lieb lattice in the three-dimensional parameter space D/J −h/J −kBT/J. The blue dome-shaped surface represents the locus of discontinuous phase transitions separating the ferrimagnetic (FRI) and disordered (DP) phases. A red critical line corresponds to continuous phase transitions between these phases.

Figure 5: Representative magnetic-field dependencies of the transition temperature of the mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1 Ising model on the Lieb lattice calculated for six selected values of the uniaxial single-ion anisotropy: (a) D/J = 1.5, (b) D/J = 1.9995, (c) D/J = 1.9997, (d) D/J = 1.9999, (e) D/J = 2.0, and (f) D/J = 2.5. The lines of discontinuous phase transitions separating the ferrimagnetically ordered phase (FRI) from the disordered phase (DP) terminate at Ising-type critical points (red circles).

Figure 6: Isothermal field dependencies of the magnetization and magnetic susceptibility of the mixed spin- 1/2 and spin-1 Ising model on the Lieb lattice as obtained from classical Monte Carlo simulations for the fixed value of the uniaxial single-ion anisotropy D/J = 1.5. The panels (a) and (b) show the single-site magnetization of the nodal (mσ) and decorating (mS ) spins together with the total magnetization (mT ) nor- malized with respect to its saturation value at two selected temperature kBT/J = 0.1 and 0.25. The panels (c) and (d) display the total magnetization and magnetic susceptibility for four selected temperatures.
